description: Return the whole memory as a compact index, one line per entity, meant to be READ ONCE AND KEPT rather than queried repeatedly. While it fits in context, searching is unnecessary: measured on a real 158-note memory, full-text search found the right note at rank 1 in 6 cases out of 10 and the index in 10 out of 10. Check `covered`: when it is false the memory is larger than the index and memory_search is still needed for what was left out.

facts_per_entity.description: how many facts to show per entity; defaults to 3

limit.description: how many entities to include; defaults to 50

covered.description: false when the memory is larger than the digest and search is still needed

title: Facts about an entity

description: Detach a source's support or remove matching facts and orphaned entities. A source-scoped call keeps facts that still have another source. Use this for what was never true -- a probe, a bad extraction, a run written under the wrong identity. For something that STOPPED being true, use memory_upsert_fact with supersedes instead: that closes the fact's window and keeps the past answerable, where this destroys it. Pass dry_run first to see the size of what you are about to remove.

dry_run.description: count what would be removed without removing it

entity.description: remove every fact touching this entity, in either direction, and the entity itself

keep_orphan_entities.description: keep entities this removal strips of their last fact

object.description: narrow to one object; cannot be used alone

predicate.description: narrow to one relation; cannot be used alone

source.description: detach support from this source run; facts with other sources remain

memory_ids.description: message or memory ids supporting this fact

run_id.description: the extraction or operator run supporting this fact

user_identifier.description: the Aura identity whose memory this is; each identity has its own database and cannot reach another's

dry_run.description: true when nothing was actually removed

entities.description: entities removed for having no facts left

facts.description: facts affected by source detachment or removal

title: Forget facts

description: Fold one entity's facts onto another and remove it, for when the same thing was recorded under two names. Prefer this over memory_forget for a duplicate: forgetting destroys the facts only the duplicate knew. If the target does not exist yet this is a rename.

source.description: the duplicate name; it is removed

target.description: the name that survives and receives the facts

user_identifier.description: the Aura identity whose memory this is; each identity has its own database and cannot reach another's

name: memory_merge_entities

dropped.description: facts discarded because they only linked the two names together

moved.description: facts re-pointed onto the surviving entity

title: Merge two entities

description: Write embedding vectors for this identity's facts. Without `all` it only fills facts that have none — the gap left by an embedder that was down. With `all` it recomputes every vector, which is what an embedding-model change requires: vectors written by a different model are in a different geometry.

all.description: recompute EVERY fact's vector, not only the facts that have none; use after the embedding model changes

batch.description: how many facts to process in one pass; defaults to 100

user_identifier.description: the Aura identity whose memory this is; each identity has its own database and cannot reach another's

name: memory_reembed

all.description: whether this pass recomputed existing vectors too

embedded.description: how many facts had a vector written

title: Recompute fact vectors

description: Find facts by their words, when you do not know which entity to ask about. If you do know the entity, call memory_facts_about instead: it is exact. Pass as_of to ask what was true at a past instant instead of what is true now. Returns no facts and marks retrieval.abstained when no candidate is relevant enough.

as_of.description: RFC3339 instant; return the facts that were valid then rather than the ones valid now

limit.description: how many facts to return; defaults to 5

query.description: what to look for, in natural language

user_identifier.description: the Aura identity whose memory this is; each identity has its own database and cannot reach another's

description: Store one fact as a bitemporal edge between two entities. A fact is never overwritten: when it is superseded its validity window is closed, so both what is true now and what was true then stay answerable.

object.description: the entity or value the subject relates to

object_kind.description: optional entity kind, e.g. Location or Organization

memory_ids.description: message or memory ids supporting this fact

run_id.description: the extraction or operator run supporting this fact

statement.description: the fact in natural language; this is what gets embedded and searched

subject.description: the entity the fact is about

subject_kind.description: optional entity kind, e.g. Person or Organization

supersedes.description: close any still-valid fact with the same subject and predicate

user_identifier.description: the Aura identity whose memory this is; each identity has its own database and cannot reach another's

valid_from.description: RFC3339 instant when the fact became true; defaults to now

valid_to.description: RFC3339 instant when the fact stopped being true; omit while it still holds

name: memory_upsert_fact

superseded.description: how many previously-valid facts had their window closed
